subject: Oceanography
title: Breaking Waves
description: Learn Breaking Waves in one minute.

hook.text: A wave breaks when it can no longer support itself—the crest outruns the base and collapses.

buildup.text: Waves break when the water depth is about 1.3 times the wave height—the bottom trips the wave.

discovery.text: There are three types: spilling (gentle slopes), plunging (steep slopes), and surging (very steep).

twist.text: Plunging breakers—the classic curling tube—release the most energy in the shortest time.

climax.text: Breaking waves move sand, erode cliffs, and generate dangerous rip currents near the shore.

punchline.text: Waves die at the shore—and their energy reshapes it.

quiz.question: When does a wave typically break?
options: When water depth is about 1.3 times the wave height
